subject.title: Sub-agent timeout recovery creates duplicate API posts (idempotency gap)

question: Should OpenClaw own durable logical-action idempotency for arbitrary sub-agent external side effects, or limit core support to gateway/message-tool retries plus plugin-provided dedupe?
rationale: The remaining behavior defines product and owner boundaries across sub-agent lifecycle, gateway RPCs, plugin APIs, external side effects, payload digest changes, and audit/replay semantics, so automation should not choose the contract alone.

options.title: Core logical-action contract
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved action identity plus claim/commit/replay state machine for sub-agent side effects and connect it to existing dedupe primitives where appropriate.

options.title: Gateway/message-tool only
options.body: Declare the current gateway and message-tool idempotency behavior as the core boundary and document that arbitrary external APIs must supply their own keys.

options.title: Plugin or ClawHub guidance only
options.body: Keep core unchanged and route safe multi-agent external side-effect patterns to plugins, skills, or operator guidance.

recommendation.title: Core logical-action contract
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved action identity plus claim/commit/replay state machine for sub-agent side effects and connect it to existing dedupe primitives where appropriate.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans gateway, agent runtime, and architecture boundaries where the history points to broad gateway/runtime ownership rather than a single plugin-local fix.
